newsitem.title: TURKEY: Istanbul gold exchange volume jumps, prices firm.
newsitem.headline: Istanbul gold exchange volume jumps, prices firm.

text.p: Volume on the Istanbul gold exchange jumped to 1,160 kilos on Tuesday from Monday's 415 as banks took advantage of the strengthening dollar in the local currency market to conduct arbitrage deals, dealers said.
Gold prices rose to $356.60 an ounce from $354.00 at Monday's close and to 1,334,100 lira per gram from 1,313,800.
The Turkish lira weakened to 116,000 against the dollar from Monday's 115,350 close due to the U.S. currency's rise in the world markets and high liquidity.

"Again the banks were conducting arbitrage deals on the market as the dollar rose in the currency market. There isn't expected to be any real physical demand until the end of Ramadan," one bank dealer said.
The Moslem holy month of Ramadan finishes on February 8 when a 3-1/2 day holiday begins.
Of the day's trade, 950 kilos was conducted in the morning session and 50.9 percent of the total was in lira terms.
